newsitem.title: CANADA: Free-trade deal with Israel passes Canadian house.
newsitem.headline: Free-trade deal with Israel passes Canadian house.

text.p: A free-trade agreement with Israel passed the Canadian Parliament's elected House of Commons on Wednesday.
The bill passed without a vote and now proceeds to the unelected Senate, where passage is usually a formality.
The agreement was signed on July 31 and will take effect on January 1 if both sides complete legislation in time.

The deal removes industrial tariffs, except on women's swimwear and certain cotton fabric. Duty-free access or low duties will be applied to a variety of agricultural and fisheries products, excluding dairy, poultry and egg products.

Canada will get better access for its grains, grain products, beef, maple sugar, alcohol and processed foods. Israel will get tariff concessions for selected fresh produce, processed foods and alcohol.
